clue.text: Deny d*** constitutes an oath

blocks.note: only the first letter of the censored word is printed, so it supplies just that letter
to constitute something is to be it
the indefinite article
a solemn promise or oath

explanation.surface: Someone insists that saying a censored swear word counts as swearing an oath.
explanation.walkthrough: The asterisked swear word really is an oath in the cursing sense, which is the joke; read literally it is 'D is a vow'.
explanation.definitionFit: To disavow a statement is to refuse to acknowledge or accept it, a straightforward synonym of rejecting or denying.

clue.text: See manager using spanner, note, prior to current workplace

blocks.note: an arch spans a gap, so it is a spanner
B is a musical note
I is the symbol for electric current
a shop, as in a workshop or shop floor

explanation.surface: A manager is spotted with a spanner, apparently heading off to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not the verb but a noun: a see is a bishop's diocese. 'Spanner' looks like a tool but means something that spans; 'prior to' places the note before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An archbishop heads an archiepiscopal see, a cathedral seat and its province, so is its chief administrator.

clue.text: Part-time physician losing a third set

indicators.note: to lose a third is to drop one third of the letters, here a middle stretch

blocks.note: Dr Jekyll was a doctor only part of the time, being Mr Hyde the rest

explanation.surface: A doctor working part-time has had a third of their hours cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Stevenson's Dr Jekyll spends part of his life as Mr Hyde, hence part-time; dropping KY, two of his six letters, leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: When a jelly or plan sets, it firms up or takes shape, which is the meaning of the verb jell.

clue.text: Organs recurring in a service vicar's organised

indicators.note: something organised has been arranged afresh, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the one letter that appears twice in 'a service'
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A vicar has arranged for organ music to feature regularly in a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organs' suggests church music, but it means body parts. Only E occurs more than once in 'a service', so that is the letter that recurs there.
explanation.definitionFit: Viscera are the internal organs of the body, especially those in the abdomen such as the intestines.

clue.text: Old-fashioned part of word that may be extracted by certain solvers

definitions.text: that may be extracted by certain solvers
definitions.note: a descriptive definition: something mathematicians extract

blocks.note: square is slang for conventional or old-fashioned
the root is the base part of a word

explanation.surface: An archaic chunk of a word is the sort of thing crossword solvers might pull out of a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'solvers' are not crossword fans but people solving equations; in mathematics one is said to extract a root.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematicians speak of extracting a square root when calculating the number that, multiplied by itself, gives a value.

clue.text: Experienced judge required trip to holy place

blocks.note: to have had something is to have experienced it
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A seasoned judge had to make a pilgrimage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Experienced' reads as an adjective for the judge, but it is a past-tense verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The hajj, also spelt hadj, is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca, a journey to Islam's holiest city.

clue.text: Fame derived from imperial position by reshuffle at top

indicators.note: a reshuffle rearranges, and 'at top' limits it to the opening letters

blocks.note: a tsardom is the rank or realm of a tsar, an emperor

explanation.surface: Someone's fame came from a top imperial job, thanks to a cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reshuffle at top' sounds political; only the first two letters swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom is the state of being a celebrity, widely known and celebrated, which is what fame describes.

clue.text: Statesman presenting one unfortunate king's identity the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means travelling backwards, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
King Lear, Shakespeare's ill-fated monarch
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: A politician gives a hapless monarch's identity incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string 'one + Lear's + ID' is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian Conservative Prime Minister, one of Britain's best-known statesmen.

clue.text: Stated amounts of liquid that can be found in minerals

definitions.text: that can be found in minerals
definitions.note: descriptive: the answer is one of the minerals

indicators.note: something stated is spoken, so the word is judged by how it is pronounced

blocks.note: quarts are measures of liquid volume

explanation.surface: Someone reports the volumes of fluid trapped inside mineral samples.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a thing found among the minerals, crystalline silica.
explanation.definitionFit: Quartz is crystalline silicon dioxide, one of the commonest rock-forming substances in the earth's crust.

clue.text: Child's complaint over silly hat in particular? Just the reverse

definitions.note: the answer is the opposite of particular

indicators.note: silly suggests muddled or foolish, so the letters are jumbled
to be over something can mean covering it all round, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: colic is a stomach ailment common in babies
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child moans about a silly hat; or rather, the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the reverse' does not reverse letters: it turns 'particular' into its opposite. Catholic in its lower-case sense means wide-ranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic tastes are broad and universal, the opposite of being particular, narrow or choosy.

clue.text: Abandon a book half-read after half one month or another

indicators.note: coming later in a sequence means placed second, so this word fixes the running order

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book
the first half of June, or equally of July
the first two of the four letters of read

explanation.surface: Someone gives up on a book halfway through, somewhere around the middle of the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or another' is fair because June and July both start the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: To abjure a belief or claim is to renounce or forswear it formally, giving it up for good.

clue.text: French rebuff lie about odd parts of their laissez-faire policy

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another
odd parts are those in the first, third and fifth places

blocks.note: non is French for no
an invention is a made-up story
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: The French say no and fib about their hands-off policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word sets up the French phrase laissez-faire, which is the definition, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Laissez-faire means letting things take their course without intervening, so it is a policy of not interfering.

clue.text: Go into hospital in stole — it gets attached to stretcher

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is held by another

blocks.note: to go into is to enter
H is the map symbol for hospital
to steal is to take, so stole is took

explanation.surface: A patient is admitted to hospital wearing a stole and lies on a stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like a wrap, but it is the past tense of steal. The stretcher is not a hospital trolley but a frame for stretching cloth, called a tenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenterhooks are the hooks that hold cloth taut on a tenter, the frame used to stretch it while drying.

clue.text: Seeking explanation for not just any old revolt

blocks.note: the definite article picks out one specific thing, unlike 'a'
O is the abbreviation for old
a rising is an uprising or revolt

explanation.surface: Historians try to account for one particular rebellion rather than any old one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not just any' describes the definite article: the, as opposed to a.
explanation.definitionFit: Theorising is forming hypotheses to account for something, which is trying to find why it happens.

clue.text: Word used comparatively often before vote, short expression of appreciation

blocks.note: than follows comparatives, as in 'bigger than'
a cross marks a vote on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A frequently used word is said just before the vote, with a brief word of gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comparatively' sounds like 'relatively', but it means with comparatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanx is an informal abbreviated spelling of thanks, the casual written way to show gratitude.

clue.text: Dutch settler caging cross dog

indicators.note: to cage something is to enclose it, so one piece shuts the other in

blocks.note: the Boers were Dutch-descended settlers in South Africa
a cross is shaped like the letter X

explanation.surface: A settler locks up an angry dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as an adjective for the dog, but it is the letter shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The boxer is a breed of medium-sized, short-haired dog originally developed in Germany.

clue.text: Following success in theatre turned up to watch very famous dancer

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up flips the letters so they read from the bottom

blocks.note: a successful show has a long run
to eye is to watch
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: After a hit show, fans turn up to see a celebrated dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very famous dancer' looks like one phrase, but 'very' supplies a letter and the definition is just 'famous dancer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Nureyev was a Soviet-born ballet star, among the most celebrated male dancers of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Our existing declaration limited cricket side — lose, in effect

indicators.note: something limited is cut short, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: what we say to announce our existence: 'we are'
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team declares its innings closed early and effectively loses.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a side may 'declare', ending its innings by choice; here the declaration is simply 'we are'. The off side is the half of the field facing the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: When a drug or feeling wears off it gradually loses its effect and fades away.

clue.text: Cleaner worked — apart from four to nine — had job in office

indicators.note: 'apart from' excludes, and 'four to nine' names the letter positions to drop

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleaner worked every hour except four till nine, as an office job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four to nine' looks like working hours, but it counts letter positions across both words.
explanation.definitionFit: To clerk is to work as a clerk, doing office administration, so clerked means held such a post.

clue.text: Loose-limbed fellows lately losing heart, as extra medicine is taken

definitions.note: describes the manner of taking a supplement

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so the middle letter goes

blocks.note: flexible and loose-limbed
fellows are men
doing something late is doing it tardily

explanation.surface: Limber men, recently out of sorts, are taking extra pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lately' usually means recently, but here it means late, tardily; its middle letter D goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplementarily means in addition, the way a supplement is taken alongside a normal diet or treatment.

clue.text: Top religious school in East with missing head

indicators.note: the head is the front, so the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism from the Far East
taken as written

explanation.surface: A top religious school in the East has lost its headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In East' is part of the description of the school, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The zenith is the highest point, whether of the sky directly overhead or of a career.

clue.text: Assessed intelligence about part of army in foreign country

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: IQ is a measured intelligence score
RA is the Royal Artillery, part of the British Army

explanation.surface: Intelligence assessments concern an army unit deployed abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Intelligence in the spy sense fits the military scene, but here it is IQ.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a Middle Eastern nation, foreign to the British setter and readers.

clue.text: Take on board again unfinished wine sailors eye

indicators.note: unfinished means lacking its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: red is a wine
ABs are able seamen
orb is a poetic word for the eye

explanation.surface: Sailors eye some half-drunk wine to bring back aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take on board' sounds nautical, matching the sailors, but it means absorb.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something on board is idiomatically to absorb or accept it, so doing it again is reabsorbing.

clue.text: Indigenous people from area in eastern part of Honshu

indicators.note: in an across-style word the east is the right-hand end, so the final letter

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written
the final letter

explanation.surface: Native people come from a region in the east of Japan's main island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ainu actually live in Hokkaido and northern Japan, so the geography adds to the surface; Honshu is Japan's largest island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ainu are the aboriginal inhabitants of northern Japan, an indigenous ethnic group distinct from the Japanese majority.

clue.text: Cricket side at Oval smoothly added to score

definitions.note: a direction written on a musical score

blocks.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field
taken as written
the letter O is drawn as an oval, so the shape stands for it

explanation.surface: A cricket team at the Oval smoothly adds runs to its score.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground, but here 'Oval' is just the shape of the letter O; the score is music, not runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is the Italian instruction marked on music telling players to perform notes smoothly and connected.

clue.text: Men committed to union securing new funds

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: fiancés are men engaged to be married
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Trade union members arrange fresh funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Committed to union' suggests trade unionists, but the union is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Finances are the money resources available to a person or organisation, which is what funds means.
